t: 3524 – Find X Value of Array I
o: Every operation keeps a contiguous remaining subarray nums[l..r] (prefix/suffix removals with both possibly empty, result non-empty), so we must count, for each residue x mod k, the number of subarrays whose product ≡ x (mod k). k ≤ 5, so residues are few: sweep r left to right keeping dp[x] = number of subarrays ending at r with product ≡ x; transition dp'[ (x·num[r]) mod k ] += dp[x], plus the singleton subarray. Accumulate into the answer each step. Example 1 verifies: [9,2,4] for k=3.
k: Remaining piece after the operation = any contiguous subarray.
k ≤ 5 ⇒ maintain counts per residue with an O(k) transition per element.
Total subarrays n(n+1)/2 acts as a sanity check.

a.i: dp[x] = number of subarrays ending at the current index with product ≡ x (mod k). Extending by num[r] maps residue x → x·num[r] mod k; adding the singleton seeds dp[num[r]%k] += 1.
s: For each element: ndp[(x*a)%k] += dp[x] for all x; ndp[a%k] += 1.
a.t: O(n·k) — constant k=5 work per element.

w: The key realization is that the operation enumerates exactly all subarrays. Counts reach n(n+1)/2 ≈ 5e9 → use 64-bit. Follow-up: the Hard version with much larger k needs a different technique (block decomposition over residues).
